dossier.public_summary: The 0.61-day dip is exactly the star's rotation period with a huge 1.4% brightness swing and a strong second eclipse about 40% as deep as the first. The long transit shape and density mismatch fit a close binary on the target, not a planet. The depth changes between sectors also match the spot variability.

reasons.why: Second dip at phase 0.2 with SNR 11.34 well above best brightening, depth ~0.4x primary, classic eclipsing binary signature.
Very large out-of-eclipse swing ~1.5x transit depth with high chi2 indicates ellipsoidal/spots from a close binary, not a planet.
Transit is twice central duration on M dwarf (rad 0.1682) with fit b essentially zero and large density penalty, inconsistent with planet orbit.

Signal period equals stellar rotation period and rotation amplitude_ppm ~13876>>depth_ppm 2533, dip is at multiple of spin period with huge variability, not a transit but the star's own variability/binary beat.
Transit shape forces stellar density far from expectation, positively favouring stellar companion over planet.
Depth changes significantly even within same pipeline, consistent with spot modulation / blended binary rather than steady planet.
